## 311ebe067559

**Reproduced defects; target left unchanged.** Audited generator SHA-256
`2b6674e389e68102a1aa93c28a4c52929051e2b7bf36906595682a11d65891a1`,
declared rule hash `e1a8e7766b84`. The assignment hash matched the inspected
bytes.

The generator advertises exact `grid_h`, `grid_w`, `n`, `palette_size`, and
`n_distinct_colors` controls but does not consume them. At seed
`5953a403a811133c874b93f1fc38ef49278e4e2122fabf4b8fca89f2fd858426:311:override`,
index 17, each low/high extreme pair produced the identical 9×11 grid with hash
`023562df2f18de5e4efb96a898e64fd526d7e919415367c47aa828b62e77427a`.
An unknown key was also accepted. Exact records are in
`checks/audit/311ebe067559/probe.json`.

**Possible training shortcut.** The canonical four pairs all contain
multiple-color ray crossings; the independent oracle matched all four, and the
“first proposal wins” rival fails 3/4 canonical pairs. Ordinary generated inputs
frequently do not require precedence:

| Band | Fixed samples | Any distinct-color crossing | Authority differs from first-wins | 3-demo sequential windows with no first-wins disagreement | Of those, query requires precedence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| easy | 1,000 | 538 | 325 | 313/997 | 94 |
| default | 1,000 | 741 | 498 | 138/997 | 63 |
| hard | 1,000 | 954 | 782 | 9/997 | 7 |

Seeds were the audit-assignment seed suffixed with `:311:<band>`, indexes
0–999. Inputs were all unique within each band and had 0 validator failures.
Sequential four-sample windows are a probe, not a claim about every downstream
lesson assembler; they demonstrate a concrete assembly policy under which the
three visible demonstrations can leave a rival alive exactly when the query
needs precedence.

A saved ordinary easy-band example (index 0) has no competing-color crossing,
passes `self_check`, belongs to the ordinary generator domain, and gives the same
output under both the real Racket authority and the rival that ignores legend
precedence and keeps the first proposal. Files:

- input and provenance: `checks/audit/311ebe067559/input.json` and
  `checks/audit/311ebe067559/generated_sample.json`;
- supported Racket application: `checks/audit/311ebe067559/racket.json`;
- rival output: `checks/audit/311ebe067559/rival_output.json`.

Racket command, from packet root:
`python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 311ebe067559 --input ../checks/audit/311ebe067559/input.json --out ../checks/audit/311ebe067559/racket.json`
(exit 0; log `checks/audit/311ebe067559/apply-command.log`).

## 311ebe067559

**A1 — Reproduced production-lesson ambiguity, not merely a suspected shortcut.**

Generator v3.0.1 SHA:
`2b6674e389e68102a1aa93c28a4c52929051e2b7bf36906595682a11d65891a1`.
Rule hash `e1a8e7766b84`; rule-source SHA:
`782a284ac4d1049955eb181444cfc18d96be143f3bec2f874b864071de4185df`.

The rule uses a first-row legend to order the priority of inward border rays;
later legend colors win overlapping rays. A rival instead takes the larger
numeric color when rays overlap. A bounded search of seeds 0..99 stopped at seed
**2**, medium, sample indices **0,1,2,3**: the first three outputs match both
rules, but the fourth differs at one output cell. This is not a claim that the
rival fits every canonical pair or the full generated distribution.

The production command with `--seed 2 --count 1 --train 3 --test 1 --difficulty
medium --allow-unapproved` produced exactly those four inputs, sample indices
and actual Racket outputs. All four inputs pass the target's validator and are
ordinary default-domain generated inputs. A second supported public apply
produced matching labels, independently of the Python candidate selector.
The wrong numeric-priority rule matches 3/3 demos and fails on the query. The
target is unapproved; this review materialization is not training admission.

**Evidence:** `checks/audit/311ebe067559/verified-counterexample.json` contains
the exact query grid, actual Racket output, rival output, differing cell,
source hashes and replay commands. `candidate.json`, `input.json`,
`racket.json` and `production.jsonl` retain the full lesson and control probe.
`checks/verify_audits.py` asserts production/Racket/Python-mirror parity for the
four lesson pairs and validates every one of the five retained audit inputs.

**A2 — Reproduced ignored exact controls.**

At seed **17**, sample **9**, medium, request
`grid_h=14, grid_w=16, palette_size=2, n_distinct_colors=2`.
The output is **8x8**, has **7 colors including background**, and is byte-for-byte
equal to the no-override output. `self_check` returns no errors. The explicit
height/width mismatch alone proves the control defect without depending on
palette terminology. This fifth grid was also accepted by public Racket apply.
The defect is that advertised requests are ignored, not that this ordinary
8x8 ray input violates the task's documented domain.

**Suggested repair direction, not applied:** add truthful observed control
contracts and ensure every training lesson includes a legend-order/numeric-order
conflict, or explicitly test that rival at assembly time. Changing labels to
numeric priority would be the wrong repair.

audits.resolution_reason: Reviewer-reported numeric-priority ambiguity and ignored generation controls; exact counterexample retained. Audited source not repaired.

## 311ebe067559

**Two existing unresolved findings freshly reproduced; audit target unchanged.**
The current `evidence/review_index.json` already records both issues as
`needs_triage`. This audit confirms their persistence against the current bytes;
it does not claim a new discovery or change their resolution.

- Generator: v3.0.1, SHA-256
  `2b6674e389e68102a1aa93c28a4c52929051e2b7bf36906595682a11d65891a1`.
- Canonical/executed rule hash: `e1a8e7766b84`.
- Executed rule-text SHA-256, as reported by public Racket apply:
  `782a284ac4d1049955eb181444cfc18d96be143f3bec2f874b864071de4185df`.

**A1 — The production lesson leaves a wrong numeric-priority rule alive.**

The canonical rule removes the first-row legend, casts inward rays from field
border emitters, preserves emitters and gray blockers, and resolves ray crossings
by the legend's order: later colors win. The retained Python rival preserves all
these behaviors except that the numerically larger color wins a crossing.

A fresh public production run at **seed 2**, **medium**, sample indices
**0, 1, 2, 3**, with **no overrides**, produces three demonstrations and one
query. The rival matches all three demonstration outputs and differs on the
query. The query's legend is `[4, 8, 2, 9, 7]`; at **zero-based output row 3,
column 7**, Racket returns **7**, while the rival returns **9**. This is the only
differing cell. A separate public Racket apply of the saved query exactly matches
the production output. The production receipt reports four attempted/accepted
pairs, zero rejections, and no declared lesson-check hook.

The Python rule mirror matches all four canonical labeled pairs; the numeric
rival fails two of those four. Thus this is a concrete ambiguity in the saved
generated lesson, not a claim that the rival solves the canonical task or every
generated lesson. No frequency estimate or seed search was performed here: seed
2 was selected from the already retained unresolved audit.

**A2 — Advertised exact controls are ignored.**

At **seed 17**, **sample index 9**, **medium**, requesting
`grid_h=14, grid_w=16, palette_size=2, n_distinct_colors=2` produces an **8×8**
grid with **five legend colors**. It is byte-for-byte equal to the same direct
generator call with no overrides. The explicit height and width mismatch proves
the defect independently of palette terminology. The saved control input also
executes successfully through public Racket apply.

**Validator and domain status.** All five unique retained generated inputs—the
four lesson inputs and the control input—return `[]` from the unchanged
`self_check`. The probe separately verifies their ordinary medium-domain
dimensions, unique left-packed legend, emitter counts and legend membership,
interior blockers, and empty remaining interior cells. They are legal ordinary
ray inputs. The control defect is the unsatisfied request. Both apply receipts
report valid outputs and matching canonical rule hashes. The task remains
unapproved with `train_safety=unverified`; this audit does not grant approval.

**Retained evidence and replay.** Paths below are relative to `WORK/`:

- `checks/audit/311ebe067559/verified-counterexample.json`: exact inputs,
  Racket/rival outputs, differing cell, validator/domain records, and source IDs.
- `checks/audit/311ebe067559/production.jsonl` and `lesson-analysis.json`: full
  production lesson, sample provenance, all demonstration comparisons.
- `checks/audit/311ebe067559/input.json`, `rival_output.json`, `racket.json`:
  query witness and independent authoritative application.
- `checks/audit/311ebe067559/control-probe.json`, `control-input.json`,
  `control-racket.json`: paired default/override witness and authoritative output.
- `checks/audit/311ebe067559/probe.py`, `canonical.json`, `canonical-rule.rkt`,
  `source-and-scope.json`: executable rival/probe and canonical/source binding.
- `checks/audit/311ebe067559/commands.json`: exact command argument arrays,
  working directories, environment override, exit codes, logs and evidence paths.

The required authoritative query command was run from the packet root, with a
temporary-directory environment setting supplied after the parent recovered
workspace inode exhaustion:

```bash
env TMPDIR=/dev/shm/arcpuzzles-205844767d55/tmp python3 review.py run python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 311ebe067559 --input ../checks/audit/311ebe067559/input.json --out ../checks/audit/311ebe067559/racket.json
```

It exited **0**. The production command, control apply, and final Python
verification also exited **0**. The wrapper's effective payload directory is
`WORK/repo`. No private runner was imported. Scope was four canonical labeled
pairs, one fixed production lesson, and one paired exact-control probe; no
battery, broad distribution sweep, or generator/rule edit was performed.

Findings-only report explicitly unresolved. Exactgrid_h/grid_w ignored, four paired requests produce identical8x8 accepted grids; control-contract issue, not label mismatch. ## 311ebe067559

**Classification: reproduced defect — advertised exact overrides are ignored.**

Audited source SHA-256:
`2b6674e389e68102a1aa93c28a4c52929051e2b7bf36906595682a11d65891a1`
(version `3.0.1`, declared rule hash `e1a8e7766b84`). No target file was edited.

The generator advertises exact `grid_h` and `grid_w` controls, but paired calls at one
fixed medium seed/index produced the same 8×8 grid in all four cases:

- `grid_h=7` and `grid_h=14` had identical SHA-256
  `125dbe10028515119f5d8f5625a0f84dc53e3975e1be577536fa86230189b437`;
  neither produced height 14.
- `grid_w=9` and `grid_w=16` produced that same grid; neither produced width 16.
- Every returned grid passed the generator's own `self_check`.

This reproduces a control-contract defect, not a semantic-rule disagreement. Evidence
and exact inputs/kwargs are in:

- `checks/audit/311ebe067559/probe.json`
- `checks/audit/311ebe067559/probe.py`
- `checks/audit/311ebe067559/probe.log`

Suggested owner action: either consume and exactly honor both axes, or remove them
from the advertised control schema; add paired override regressions that assert the
requested dimensions and output inequality when values differ.

triage.reason: Both source-bound control/distribution findings explicitly unresolved; no target edits or approval updates.
